definitions.explanation: A comprehensive philosophy or outlook on the world and one's place in it.
The overall atmosphere, rules, and setting of a creative work such as a novel, game, anime, or film. Very commonly used in discussions of fiction and media in Japanese.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{世界観|せかいかん}は{独特|どくとく}だ。
{旅|たび}を{通|とお}して{世界観|せかいかん}が{変|か}わった。
{宗教|しゅうきょう}はその{人|ひと}の{世界観|せかいかん}に{大|おお}きな{影響|えいきょう}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: Religion has a major influence on a person's worldview.

examples.japanese: このゲームの{世界観|せかいかん}が{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like the world-setting of this game.

examples.japanese: {原作|げんさく}の{世界観|せかいかん}を{忠実|ちゅうじつ}に{再現|さいげん}した{映画|えいが}だ。
examples.english: It's a film that faithfully recreates the world of the original work.

examples.japanese: ファンタジー{作品|さくひん}では、まず{世界観|せかいかん}をしっかり{作|つく}り{込|こ}むことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: In fantasy works, it's important to first build a thorough world-setting.

notes:
{世界観|せかいかん} has two distinct uses in modern Japanese.

Sense 1 (philosophical worldview) is the original meaning, corresponding to the German "Weltanschauung."

Sense 2 (fictional world-setting) is extremely common in pop culture discussions. When fans talk about a game, anime, or novel's {世界観|せかいかん}, they mean its atmosphere, rules, lore, and overall creative vision.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {世界観|せかいかん}が{広|ひろ}がる (the world expands)
- {世界観|せかいかん}を{作|つく}り{込|こ}む (build out a world-setting in detail)
- {世界観|せかいかん}を{壊|こわ}す (break the world-setting / ruin the atmosphere)
- {独特|どくとく}な{世界観|せかいかん} (a unique worldview/world-setting)
